transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-03-05 16:00 UTC | Duration: 58 minutes | Recording ID: ff-20260305-BH-01
Attendees: Avery Chen (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Marco Diaz (Redwood CSM); Dana Lee, Omar Ruiz, Samantha Park, Raj Patel (BlueHarbor)

Summary: Kickoff/orientation for onboarding sprint. Covered scope (pilot use cases: customer support triage + freight ETA summarization), environment choices (hosted vs dedicated vs private), security requirements (SSO, KMS, audit logs), scheduling milestones and initial perf/QA plan. Agreed next steps and owners.

Topics: onboarding timeline; security/compliance; deployment options and tradeoffs; performance validation; success metrics + roll out plan

Action items (brief): see metadata actions.

Transcript body:
00:00 Avery (Redwood): Hey everyone thanks for joining, we're on the 4pm slot — appreciate you squeezing this in. Intro from our side: I'm Avery, I'll own the account and cadence. Priya is our SE who will run the private deployment checklist. Marco will help with onboarding and cost telemetry.
00:18 Dana: Thanks Avery — hi all, I'm Dana, head of AI for BlueHarbor. Quick context: we want to pilot two workflows — support ticket triage to auto-summarize and a freight ETA summarization for our ops teams. Budget is tight, timeline target is end of Q2.
00:35 Avery: Great. Can you remind us what your infra looks like today? Kubernetes? On prem? Cloud?
00:44 Omar: We're on AWS, EKS for control plane, some services in GCP. We have a shared VPC with strict egress rules. We want either VPC peering or Private link. On-prem is not in scope for pilot but might be later.
01:02 Priya: okay makes sense, for the pilot we can do Redwood Hosted to move fast or Redwood Dedicated in your VPC for more deterministic throughput. Tradeoffs: hosted = fastest to start, less ops; dedicated = reserved GPUs, predictable latency but needs networking set-up.
01:22 Raj: Latency matters for triage, we need sub-300ms tail for short prompts. Cost matters more for nightly bulk summarization. How do you usually balance that?
01:36 Marco: We typically recommend a hybrid — route latency-critical requests to a lower-latency dedicated pool and batch night jobs through a cheaper quantized model. We can show cost per 1M tokens for both.
01:54 Samantha: Quick security question — we need SOC2 evidence, SSO via Okta, and customer-managed keys (KMS). Also audit logs must be retained for 12 months.
02:06 Priya: Yes, we support SAML/Okta SSO, and for Private deployments we can integrate your KMS/HSM. Audit logs are available; retention can be configured via our console or exported to your S3. We'll share the SOC2 pack and the private deployment questionnaire.
02:24 Dana: Also curious about KV cache — we have many similar prompts with session state. Does Redwood cache prefixes automatically or do we need to add logic?
02:36 Priya: We have automatic prefix and KV caching options but the transcript here might show read-wood KV as 'KV cash' sometimes in older docs — but yes it's built in. For long-running sessions we'll recommend explicit keying strategy. We'll include an example config.
02:58 Raj: Any reason to avoid the hosted path? We like to go fast but worried about PII transmitted.
03:07 Avery: Hosted stores short-term context and you can opt-in to never-log mode. For regulated data we usually recommend Dedicated with VPC or Private for full control. The team should decide by the end of week for the sprint plan.
03:25 Omar: What about throughput — we want to run a batch job that processes 500k lines overnight. Will that be a problem on Dedicated?
03:36 Priya: Not at all; Dedicated pools can be sized. For big batch jobs we suggest configuring autoscaling and a cheaper quantized model variant. We'll give a sample sizing plan.
03:52 Dana: Regarding metrics — what are the success criteria for pilot?
04:00 Marco: We should define: 1) accuracy and human evaluator score for 1k test prompts; 2) latency SLO (P95/P99) for triage; 3) cost per 10k interactions. Also adoption metrics like % of support tickets auto-summarized after 4 weeks.
04:22 Samantha: Compliance: can you provide an ATO-like checklist? We need network flow diagrams and an assurance that logs are tamper-evident.
04:32 Priya: We'll export the audit log schema and retention options and include a recommended logging funnel into your SIEM. We'll also provide a network template for peering.
04:46 Dana: Any competitors or existing vendor lock we should note? Our infra team previously evaluated RivalAI and CloudModel Inc — they had higher managed costs or required more custom infra.
04:59 Avery: Noted. We'll include a comparative slide in the runbook with a cost/latency tradeoff.
05:06 Raj: Who will be the day-to-day contact for the pilot?
05:10 Marco: Marco will manage weekly check-ins, Priya will handle infra, Avery will handle commercial questions.
05:15 Dana: OK. Can we walk through the sprint milestones?
05:18 Avery: Yes — rough plan: week 0 (this week): finalize scope and sign-off on networking; week 1: provisioning + smoke tests; week 2: integration with ticketing and data pipelines; week 3: evals and adjust; week 4: go/no-go and handoff to product ops. We can compress if you want a faster timeline.
05:45 Omar: We might need an extra week for networking approvals. Do you have a templated network diagram to speed sign-off?
05:52 Priya: Yes, we'll attach a VPC template and security group example. Link: https://redwood.example.com/onboarding/runbook-blueharbor (note: sample link in transcript).
06:05 Samantha: Regarding KMS, we use AWS KMS with asymmetric keys. Any blockers?
06:12 Priya: Supported. For Private we can integrate; for Dedicated we can accept envelope encryption with your KMS. We'll add a small writeup.
06:22 Dana: Perf testing — can Redwood run a 10k qps synthetic test or do we run it?
06:30 Marco: We can coordinate — Redwood can spin a load generator in a staging pool and share the results. For the pilot we suggest a 2k sustained qps smoke and a 10k spike test.
06:45 Raj: Any gotchas we should watch for? We've got lots of short prompts which sometimes cause attention blowouts.
06:52 Priya: Watch tokenization and sequence length distribution; also warm KV cache can help. We'll share token histogram tooling.
07:05 Dana: Ok next steps recap?
07:08 Avery: I'll send the runbook, sprint calendar, and a short cost baseline. Priya will send the private deployment questionnaire and the network template. Marco will schedule weekly 30-min syncs starting next Tuesday. Samantha will share SSO and KMS vendor details. Omar will provide egress/VPC info by next Tuesday.
07:35 Samantha: We'll try to get the docs to you earlier.
07:38 Marco: I'll put meeting invites for the weekly check-in and the infra deep-dive.
07:45 Avery: Any final Qs?
07:49 Dana: No, thanks. Looking forward to the kickoff.
07:52 Avery: Great, thanks everyone.

References mentioned (links): onboarding runbook (https://redwood.example.com/onboarding/runbook-blueharbor), SOC2 summary (attached in follow-up), private-deploy-questionnaire (link to doc to be shared).

End of recording.
